issues.rationale: Added a separate structural row for both exact filenames and all three required workbook sheet names, then reallocated four integer points without changing the 58-point total.
Removed the named SKU answers and now judge completeness against a disclosed, source-grounded risk rule applied consistently to the catalog.
The temporal-selection criterion now accepts either latest non-missing values by indicator or the latest complete common year when the policy is stated and consistently applied.
Added a separate structural row for the three exact filenames, instructed formats, and exact five-sheet workbook set while preserving the 50-point total.

The defect is absent judge access to the portfolio, framework, application, CDFI, FDIC, and concentration sources. Embedding their expected populations, weights, thresholds, or answers in the rubric would recreate hidden-answer scoring.

Affinity inputs, vibration points, standard limits, bearing geometry, spectra, and IOM guidance must be supplied to deterministic checks or the judge; encoding them in rubric text would leak expected answers.

Verification requires normalized design inputs, controlled ASME chart and material data, and calculation checks. The rubric already permits documented uncertainty and should not embed authoritative chart values or expected conclusions.

The judge needs the complete inquiry, catalog, Shopify, and review datasets or deterministic join and ranking outputs. The hidden SKU hints were removed rather than expanded into a canonical answer list.
Chart and conditional-format visibility is an XLSX rendering or object-inspection limitation. The visualization requirement is explicit in the task and remains in the rubric.

Cleaning, source extraction, annex parsing, imputation, typology, and regression verification require source extracts and deterministic recomputation. The rubric was made method-neutral but does not encode expected source rows or model outputs.

Exact codebook names, benchmark values, source coverage, and statistical results require normalized external and local sources. Adding those expected values to rubric text would undermine task-instruction alignment.

The 500-row SQLite extraction cap prevents full-table inspection. This requires full-table summaries, targeted flagged-row extraction, or a higher scoped limit, not hidden respondent IDs or corrections in the rubric.

The similarity dimensions and thresholds must now derive from escalated-product indicators and/or the catalog distribution. The rule is applied to every non-escalated SKU, all matches are shown, and a no-match result requires a full-catalog comparison.
